I've asked claude opus for some tips, I've had the same issues with claude code so in my case it's not specific to OpenCode. I've disabled resource saver to see if that helps, but I'm going to continue tomorrow and see if that helped.

---

Most Likely Causes & Fixes

  1. Docker Desktop (if installed)

  This is a very common cause. Docker's Resource Saver mode conflicts with WSL 2.5.1+ (cgroupv2).

  Fix: Disable Resource Saver in Docker Desktop:
  - Docker Desktop → Settings → Resources → Advanced → Disable "Resource Saver"

  Or close Docker Desktop entirely to test if it's the cause.

  2. Restart LxssManager Service

  From Windows (Run as Admin PowerShell):
  Restart-Service LxssManager
  Or: Open services.msc → Find "LxssManager" → Restart it. Also set it to Automatic startup.

  3. Force kill and restart WSL

  # From PowerShell
  taskkill /f /im wslservice.exe
  wsl --shutdown
  wsl

  4. Create/update .wslconfig

  Create %UserProfile%\.wslconfig with:
  [wsl2]
  memory=8GB
  swap=4GB
  localhostForwarding=true

  5. Quick temporary fix when frozen

  When it happens: Press Ctrl+C, then Ctrl+/- (zoom in/out) - this sometimes unsticks it.

  ---
  Do you have Docker Desktop installed? That's the most common culprit for this exact symptom pattern.

  Sources:
  - https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/17096
  - https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/10378
  - https://github.com/docker/for-win/issues/14656

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #2202: PATH is not inherited from invoking shell
- #4968: Shell sessions losing $PATH value from parent shell

These issues describe the root cause of why mise binaries aren't found in the desktop app - the PATH environment variable isn't properly inherited from the parent shell. Adding mise support would likely be resolved by fixing the underlying PATH inheritance issue.

Feel free to ignore if your specific case requires additional consideration.

I'm just thankful I've seen so many LLM powered responses talking about empathy from what are clearly accounts held by non-technical people who have never done anything without an LLM holding their hand. It gives me hope that someday robots can actually perform that as a service as well.

From my perspective, the people that abused the API key and intentionally set up their stuff knowing that they were going to go over their limit to intentionally commit fraud by abusing the open code platform to throw the entire open code community under the bus are the problem here, because they did so simply so they could get free token usage and did not care that by doing that they were making the opencode community look like it was adversarial to the model providers that it depends on.

My honest guess guess is a lot of you are going to get banned from using Anthropic models if you haven't been already. Most of you have no empathy and that's why you're not thinking about how this impacts the relationship with opencode and other providers, or how it could limit the ability to gain access to models or the goodwill to allow opencode to simply have a provider for a service in the future with it being a problem that harms Access for everybody else down the line.

In simple english, The fact that Anthropic even had to do this severely hurts the reputation of the opencode community and makes it seem more darknet friendly than it should be.  The opencode leadership needs to dramatically sway away from this, be public about the problem, and actively support what Anthropic did or it will lose legitimacy with every other provider.

This is one of the reasons why you should all be thinking about empathy and trying to be a good and collaborative player in the ecosystem instead of forcing things or trying to extract value forcefully. You are critically dependent on API access to access their models and this time all they did was cut off one client they didn't remove your entire account like they could have.

Like I said, Anthropic is being very chill about this and you should be appreciative and empathetic of that.

It's easy to ask other people to be empathetic when you're not the one being harmed, But I challenge you all to be more empathetic when you're the one losing out, And I challenge you to understand that if this makes opencode adversarial with anthropic, it could create bad blood with other providers and that's not what you want, either. Yes, it's open source, and open source can be good, but it needs to be maintained legitimacy, in order to maintain itself, because if it becomes this rogue software project that attempts to extract free resources from API's as a dark client (as is currently being claimed by some of you) when it's not allowed to be, then it will just be declared a hacking tool and deleted by GitHub, and at that point Anthropic will stop being so chill. 

Every single one of you that's trying to get past the security that anthropic has put up is actively putting the open source community and this project at risk, and need to stop.

I don't think anybody wants Anthropic to show their teeth here; It's not like they don't know who owns the API keys that are being billed.

Just accept that this was a security hole that has since been fixed, and move on with your life, is my greatest advice here, and that is why I'm going to be muting this thread.

Perhaps I misunderstand the intent of this post, but it seems to paint the community with an incredibly broad brush while ignoring a massive segment of the user base: those of us who are paying Anthropic customers.

I have been a developer since the late 90s, and I’ve seen the industry evolve through several paradigm shifts. Today, tools like Claude are transformative because they allow me to operate as an architect and orchestrator rather than being bogged down strictly with the syntax of every line of code. To maintain that level of high-level orchestration, I've come to enjoy a flexible interface that fits my workflow . . . which is exactly why I use OpenCode.

I pay $100+ a month for a Max-tier subscription. I am not trying to "extract free value" or "commit fraud." I am trying to use the compute I pay for through a tool that supports my professional output. The idea that using a third-party client is somehow "adversarial" or "darknet-adjacent" is a bizarre take that fundamentally mischaracterizes why many of us are here.

Again, apologies if I completely misunderstand your intent, but, at an initial read-through, I completely disagree.

I've found the issue. Apparently OpenCode also looks at folders higher in the folder structure for opencode.json. 
ie
~/Projects/MyApp/opencode.json
~/Projects/opencode.json

Run opencode in
cd ~/Projects/MyApp/
opencode .
Finds ~/Projects/opencode.json and uses it, which contained the temperature and top_k definitions.
